findings.finding: Step 5 makes non-git → SKIP, directly contradicting the unit spec: "unobtainable diff, collector unavailable, regeneration failure → STOP with a remediation (never the lazy-loader SKIP). Applies at every complexity." The spec explicitly closes the lazy-SKIP loophole; the mini-plan reopens it for the non-git case, which is precisely the environment where a lazy-loaded agent most often lands.
findings.suggestion: Non-git / no merge-base / no commit → STOP with remediation, matching the spec. Only complexity-tier gating may vary, never the failure modes.  2. Category: dependency — Severity: high

findings.finding: Step 1 changes collector semantics (`_file_tags.py` gains multi-line folding, class/module-level tag binding, dedupe of propagated hits). The base manifest is a frozen artifact read through `_keystone_base_manifest.py`. If the base manifest was generated by the old collector, head-vs-base comparison becomes inconsistent: e.g., a suite-tag-inheriting test counts as untagged in base but tagged in head, corrupting the untagged-added delta. The mini-plan never mentions regenerating or version-pinning the base manifest against the new collector.
findings.suggestion: Either regenerate the base manifest with the new collector in this same change (and state the coordinate), or record a collector-semantics version in the manifest and STOP on mismatch. Add a test asserting base and head go through the same collector path.  3. Category: risk — Severity: medium

findings.finding: Any behavior change to `_file_tags.py` also feeds `_layer_coverage_regen`'s removal gate and coverage ratchet downstream. Folding multi-line `test(` heads could change tag counts for existing files, shifting coverage numbers mid-campaign.
findings.suggestion: Include before/after manifest diff on HEAD as a test: the change should only add tags for previously-unbound multi-line/suite-tag cases; any other delta is a bug. Note the expected delta in the PR.  4. Category: edge-case — Severity: medium

findings.finding: Move-matching by normalised body digest has a collision problem: multiple identical or near-identical tests (common with generated/parametrised-template tests and legacy copy-paste) share a digest. Matching one head test against "base tests that vanished in changed files" is then ambiguous — greedy matching order determines whether a test reads as new (STOP) or moved (pass).
findings.suggestion: Define a deterministic match (e.g., prefer same-file-path, then same name, then digest) and add a test with two identical-bodied tests moved to different files. Also handle many-to-one (base digest matched twice).  5. Category: risk — Severity: medium

findings.finding: The evidence-free head memoisation is shared between the removal gate and this gate, but the invalidation story is unstated. If the cache is keyed by anything weaker than the exact head commit (e.g., process lifetime, or "latest run"), a second verify in the same process after a commit could reuse a stale head manifest and silently pass/fail wrongly.
findings.suggestion: Key the head memo on the resolved head SHA; assert the key on read and treat a mismatch as cache miss.  6. Category: security / correctness — Severity: medium

findings.finding: fixture-or-helper` exemptions hinge on a static `would_collect` approximation of pytest's collection rules. Pytest collection is subtle (custom `python_functions`, conftest `collect_ignore`, `__init__.py` package semantics, `Test` classes with `__init__` being skipped). A wrong `would_collect` grants a silent exemption — a bypass of the gate.
findings.suggestion: Document the specific rules `would_collect` implements, prefer reading `python_functions`/`python_classes` from the project config where cheap, and add tests for the known traps (`Test` with `__init__`, `collect_ignore` at minimum acknowledged as unsupported → fail closed with a comment).  7. Category: edge-case — Severity: medium

findings.finding: mechanical-refactor`'s identifier-anonymised digest makes identifier renames invisible wholesale. A "rename" that collides with an existing symbol (e.g., renaming a local to shadow or alias a different imported symbol) is a real behavior change that would pass the gate.
findings.suggestion: Require that the anonymised digest equality holds and the set of imported/referenced module-level names is unchanged, or at least flag collisions as a WARN with the exemption still passing. Low cost, closes the main bypass.  8. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: Carry-over #2 adds `except SystemExit` to `run_claim_checks`; `SystemExit` carries a code (`exit(0)` vs `exit(1)`). Blanket-catching it and reporting as a crashed check changes behaviour for checks that legitimately call `sys.exit(0)` on success.
findings.suggestion: Treat `SystemExit` with non-zero/None code as a crash; verify no existing check exits 0 as a success path.  9. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: TS digest drops trailing commas and comments after the title; generator-sourced Playwright tests with template-literal titles or `.each` tables may produce bodies whose digest differs spuriously on reformats, causing false untagged-modified STOPs on legacy tests.
findings.suggestion: Add a test for a `.each`-table test touched by formatter-only changes; if it fails, restrict untagged-modified to tests that appear in both base and head of the same file with digest change — which the plan already implies — and confirm formatting-only churn normalises away.

findings.finding: Step 5’s non-git → SKIP contradicts the explicit requirement that an unobtainable diff must STOP at every complexity. It would let the gate disappear precisely when it cannot establish a baseline.
findings.suggestion: Return STOP with remediation for non-git execution, and test that behavior through F11.

findings.finding: Identifier-anonymised digest equality is insufficient to validate `mechanical-refactor`. It can accept behavioral changes such as replacing one called function with another or swapping variable references, because both bodies become identical after anonymisation.
findings.suggestion: Validate the body difference against a consistent rename mapping that preserves identifier relationships and scope. Test rejected call substitutions and variable swaps alongside the required 200-test rename.

findings.finding: Folding multiline `test`/`it`/`describe` heads before parsing can alter strings, comments, or source locations unless the transformation understands those boundaries. The plan also does not explain how nested suite tags reach individual tests. Both affect the shared production collector.
findings.suggestion: Keep this within the existing collector’s parsing path, preserve original source locations, and explicitly cover nested suite inheritance and multiline calls containing comments or string delimiters. Verify existing collector output remains stable.

findings.finding: A separate static `would_collect` implementation risks disagreeing with the production collector about test roots, configured naming patterns, class methods, and fixture exclusions. That disagreement could incorrectly grant `fixture-or-helper` exemptions.
findings.suggestion: Use the production collector’s collected identities and discovery rules as the authority. Treat uncertain collection status as STOP rather than permitting an exemption, and cover configured roots and production `test_.py` modules.

findings.finding: The authoring step mentions an F12 share line, but the contract also requires exemption count and share in the PR body and campaign’s final measurement. Those output changes and their denominator are unspecified.
findings.suggestion: Identify and update all three producers, define the share denominator consistently, and verify that missing legacy records remain distinguishable from recorded zero exemptions in F12 and the PR body.  The overall approach is sound: it reuses the production collector, manifest regeneration, and extracted verifiers. These specific contract and exemption-validation gaps need correction before implementation; repository inspection was blocked, so this review is based on the supplied specification and mini-plan.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

doubt.disposition: blocker 1 (no Agent tool): Stage 3 runs only behind a Stage 2 pass, and the internal cascade did not run in this campaign sub-iterate

findings.finding: The new tests use `inspect.getfile`, `re.search`, `Path`, `monkeypatch`/`tmp_path` and `claims`, but the diff adds no imports to this file — the hunk only appends after line 101. Unless `inspect` and `re` were already imported (nothing in the visible file uses them before), `test_no_registered_check_module_imports_iterate_checks` and the crashed-check test raise `NameError` at collection/run time.
findings.suggestion: Verify/add `import inspect`, `import re` (and `from pathlib import Path` if absent) at the top of the file; run the suite to confirm.

findings.finding:
_CALLBACK_RE` searches for `=>` or the word `function` anywhere in a line, including inside the test title string or the options object. A correctly tagged wrapped test such as `test(
  'verifies the login function works',
  { tag: ['@FR-02.01'] },
  async ({ page }) => {...` ends its "head" at the title line (the word `function` matches there), leaving `{ tag: [...] }` unjoined — the grammar then cannot bind the tag and the gate false-STOPs a correctly tagged test. Same for a title containing `=>`.
findings.suggestion: Only treat a line as the callback line when the match is outside a string literal (e.g. strip string literals per line before matching, or require the line to end with `=>`/`function (` shape).

findings.finding: Warnings (a tag outside the run's expected FRs, or an unused exemption) produce `CheckResult(..., ok=False, severity=WARNING)`. The spec says these cases WARN, not STOP. If any caller branches on `ok` alone (the integration test itself asserts `result.ok is True` on the happy path, implying `ok=False` is a failure), a mere warning blocks the run — in particular an exemption recorded for a test that legitimately ended up passing (unused) would fail the gate. Confirm the WARNING severity is genuinely non-blocking in the F11 pipeline; if it isn't, this is a false STOP path.
findings.suggestion: Either return `ok=True` with the warning text, or verify/ensure the report renderer treats `severity == WARNING` as non-blocking, and add a test for the unused-exemption case at the gate level.

findings.finding: read` returning `""` (file absent/unreadable-as-empty) is mapped to `()` ("no such test") instead of an infra failure. In `_flag`'s `untagged-modified` branch, `before=()` vs a real head digest then emits "body changed, still no requirement tag" — an unreadable base file is reported as a test defect rather than the spec-mandated "cannot read → STOP with remediation" infra failure. The `if text else ()` also conflates a genuinely empty file with "absent".
findings.suggestion: Distinguish empty/absent from unreadable at the reader contract level, and flag unreadable base-side files as a "cannot read the file to compare bodies" finding (the head side already does this).

findings.finding: The join runs on raw source with no string-literal awareness, so a line inside a multi-line template literal (or a chained call ending in `test(` / `it(` / `describe(` as a plain identifier, e.g. `run.filter(it(`) that happens to end with an open paren gets folded with following lines, corrupting string contents and titles for both the tag parser and the untagged enumeration.
findings.suggestion: Cheap mitigation: require the matched identifier to be preceded by a statement start / `;` / `}` / `)` boundary, or skip joining when the line is inside an unclosed template literal.

findings.finding: Module-level `pytestmark` is bound to every `test` function found via `ast.walk` over all top-level statements — including `test` methods of non-`Test` helper classes and nested helper functions pytest would never collect. That inflates the manifest's tag links (and can make a helper look "tagged"), diverging from collection truth the rest of the gate relies on.
findings.suggestion: Restrict `_test_names` for the `pytestmark` case to module-level functions plus methods of `Test` classes, matching `would_collect`'s rules.

findings.finding: The printed "exempted M of K added/edited tests" uses `K = tagged_new + exempted`, which excludes still-failing untagged additions, moved tests, and edited-legacy untagged tests — so K under-counts the added/edited set the spec's F12 share is defined over.
findings.suggestion: Compute K from the union of `tagged_new`, `exempted`, failing `untagged-added`/`untagged-modified` findings and (optionally) `moved`.

findings.finding: The cached head manifest dict is returned by reference to multiple gates per run; only a docstring ("callers must not mutate") protects it. Any future/hidden mutation (e.g. by `require_manifest_shape` normalization or evidence folding) poisons the second consumer silently.
findings.suggestion: Return a `copy.deepcopy` of the cached manifest (it's built once per run; the copy cost is trivial next to the ~11 s regeneration).

findings.finding: Class marks produce IDs containing only the method name. If tagged `TestLogin.test_success` and untagged `TestLogout.test_success` share a file, the propagated tag identifies both as `file::test_success`. The untagged test can therefore pass the gate without proving a tagged requirement.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the enclosing class in collector IDs and body matching. Add an integration test with identically named methods in tagged and untagged classes.

findings.finding: Fixture exclusion applies to untagged tests, but not to invalid or unresolved tags. Adding a deliberately malformed tag under `tests/fixtures/` produces a STOP unless the project separately configures collector exclusions. The specification requires these trees to be excluded automatically; the integration test masks this by supplying `exclude_dirs`.
findings.suggestion: Apply the fixture exclusion consistently to tag findings, preferably in the shared collector inventory. Test a malformed fixture repository without explicit exclusion configuration.

findings.finding: The exemption denominator excludes edited tests that already have valid tags, and legacy tests newly given tags. For example, one exempted legacy edit plus nine tagged edits reports “exempted 1 of 1 … (100%)” instead of 1 of 10 (10%). This makes the required F12 and PR measurement inaccurate.
findings.suggestion: Track all added or body-modified test identities independently of whether they produce findings or new links, and calculate the share from that inventory.

findings.finding: Out-of-scope warnings are restricted to tests absent from `base_ids`. Adding an unrelated FR tag to an existing test—or tagging an edited legacy test with an unrelated FR—does not WARN, although the contract applies to every new tag outside the iterate’s expected FR set.
findings.suggestion: Compare base and head tag bindings as `(FR, test)` pairs and warn on newly introduced bindings outside the expected set.

findings.finding: A non-git project returns a successful SKIP when no diff can be obtained. The specification explicitly requires an unobtainable diff to STOP; it provides no non-git exception. The new test enshrines behavior contrary to that failure contract.
findings.suggestion: Return a blocking result with remediation for `not_git`, and update the test to require STOP.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The implementation follows the intended collector architecture, but tag identity can permit untagged tests through, and several enforcement and reporting requirements remain incomplete. Workspace commands were blocked by policy, so this review used the supplied diff and specification without running tests or reading the authoritative brief.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
